## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekakapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.1) is a chapter of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the fourth book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text sets out definitions and classifications of individual types of persons [Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka]. For example, near the beginning of the chapter, it treats categories such as the person "liberated at times" (*samayavimutta*)—who abides contacting the eight deliverances with the body from time to time and destroys taints by seeing with wisdom—and the person "liberated not at times" (*asamayavimutta*) [Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka]. In broader Pali Buddhist exegesis, the *Puggalapaññatti* is the only text among the seven Abhidhamma treatises to supply passages directly referenced by commentators in discussions of the dry-insight practitioner (*sukkhavipassaka*) [Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka].
